Ben — thanks again for the demo this morning. We have a week to finalize the POC sizing and want Redwood Dedicated to host inference for a multimodal pipeline (clinical notes + images). High-level profile:
- Peak concurrent QPS: 55 (short spikes to ~120 for <10s)
- Typical request mix: 60% text-only short-context (<=512 tokens), 40% multimodal where the text + image produces 2–3k token internal context due to retrieved context.

Attached: catalyst_poc_qps_profile.csv and Catalyst security checklist. Curious on your recommendation: H100 vs A100 vs L4? Also we have a small on-prem inference server pool (NVIDIA A100 40GB) for a subset of sensitive records — can Redwood mix in cross-region or private capacity for fallthrough?

Alice — appreciate the profile and attachments. High-level quick take before we finalize a tiling plan:

- L4 (single-socket 24–32GB class) is extremely cost-efficient for the text-only 60% of traffic and will hit p50 << 80ms if you use a trimmed model (short context optimized). However, L4 struggles with long-context multimodal sequences and large KV cache size needs.
- A100 (40GB) is a good middle ground — better memory headroom for 2–3k tokens with reasonable perf; can handle mixed traffic with fewer model variants. If you quantize to q4/q5 it can be highly cost-effective.
- H100 is the high-performance option for very low p95 on long contexts (and large batch throughput). It gives the best latency for the multimodal path but at a material price premium. H100 also reduces tail variance under short burst spikes thanks to better tensor core throughput.

Given the POC constraints (tight budget, need to show p95 multimodal <400ms), a blended strategy typically wins: prioritize L4 for steady text traffic + A100 for multimodal; reserve H100 only if measured latency on A100 misses p95 targets during a controlled pilot.

I'll loop in Marissa and Dev to sketch a concrete fleet-tiling spreadsheet (slots per SKU, fallback policy, burst mix) and an ops plan for KV cache sizing and mem headroom. Is next Tue 9/14 10a PT OK for a short cadence call?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Forwarding Alice's profile — draft notes below (will attach a quick tiling workbook):

Key unknowns requiring validation from CatalystBio:
- Exact tokenization blowup for image-derived context (they quoted 2–3k but need distribution).
- Whether the most sensitive subset must always execute on customer on-prem A100s (data residency).
- If they will accept quantized variants of the production model during POC (q4/q5).

Draft fleet tiling proposal (POC month):
1) Baseline steady-state: 8 x L4 nodes (serve short-context traffic, ~6K steady QPS capacity after batching).
2) Multimodal pool: 6 x A100-40GB nodes (pin larger KV cache, handle 40% load and 95% of multimodal requests).
3) Burst reserve: 2 x H100 nodes on dedicated standby (auto-burst trigger > 90 concurrent multimodal QPS or p95 degradation).

Operational notes:
- KV cache per A100 node: provisioned to support avg 3k token contexts * 20 concurrent users ~ 120k token frames. Example: recommend 320GB total KV memory per A100 host (prefer multiples for headroom).
- Autoscaling: prefer slot-based scaling (increment by 1-2 nodes) with immediate fallback routing to H100 when queue latency > 50ms for >10s.
- Fallback policy: multimodal -> A100 primary, fallback -> H100; text-only -> L4, fallback -> A100 if L4 cold-cache miss and latency spike persists >30s.
- Cost estimate (month of POC, rough): L4 pool ~$6.5k, A100 pool ~$48k, H100 standby (2 nodes reserved burst) ~$28k. Total ~ $82.5k (compute-only).

Next steps from our side: Dev to validate memory estimates and tiling workbook, Karthik to draft contract clause for burst pricing and SLA during POC. Ben to confirm call with Alice.

-Marissa
Product Lead, Dedicated Capacity

Thanks — quick technical checks from infra:
- Memory math: "320GB KV per A100 host" is an ok thumb rule but we should express as number of cache shards and max tokens per shard. For 3k token contexts, 320GB buys ~100 shards at 3k tokens each (including metadata), which gives us 20 concurrent sessions per shard comfortably.
- Model variants: we should plan for 3 variants: text-opt (L4, int8/q4), balanced (A100 q5), long-context (A100/H100 fp16 or q4nf). That avoids repeated model swaps at inference time.
- Cold-starts: L4 is cheap but suffers higher cold-cache misses for multimodal; we must proactively warm frequently accessed keys during POC via synthetic requests. Ops will add a warm-up lambda that runs on 1-min cadence.
- Integration with Catalyst's on-prem A100s: yes, we can set a routing tag so that requests with high-sensitivity headers route to customer-managed endpoints first; if unavailable, Redwood Dedicated falls back per policy (with audit log of fallbacks for compliance).

I'll update the workbook with shard counts, reserve buffer, and an ops playbook. Estimated dev time: ~2 d to produce a runnable pilot config.

-Dev
Senior Infra Engineer
